title: Monica Lewinsky has one request for critics nearly 30 years after White House scandal
summary: Monica Lewinsky wishes critics would get new jokes after nearly three decades, sharing on a podcast how she reshaped public perception of her own story.
story: Activist Monica Lewinsky told Fox News Digital that her personal definition of power has evolved over the years.
Monica Lewinsky has evolved since the White House scandal – and she hopes critics one day can, too.
Lewinsky, 53, credited time and patience as her saving graces while reflecting on challenges from her past during an appearance on the "All the Cool Girls" podcast.
"I think that coming into my 50s was amazing and just the shedding of worries," she told co-hosts Laura Brown and Kristina O'Neill.
MONICA LEWINSKY'S LINDSEY GRAHAM TRIBUTE DRAWS CRITICISM AND PRAISE FOR PLACING PEOPLE OVER PARTY: EXPERT
Monica Lewinsky reclaimed her own narrative years after a White House scandal. (Monica Schipper)

"I mean that whole … joke about 'I don't give anymore f---s,' and it's like you really start to give fewer and fewer f---s, and you settle into acceptance in a way that has been really reassuring for me."
Unlike the critics, the podcast host moved on from past discretions to reclaim not only her life, but also her own story.
"In terms of the people who still have old, old beliefs, I wish they would get some new jokes because, I mean, 30 years of the same jokes, Jesus," she said. "Or 28 years. We're not at 30 yet."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Monica Lewinsky pleaded for critics to find a new joke nearly 30 years after her highly-publicized scandal. (Amy Sussman/Getty Images)

Lewinsky was 21 years old when she began an unpaid internship at the White House in July 1995. She turned 22 that summer, and her sexual relationship with former President Bill Clinton, who was 49 at the time, began in November 1995.

It was only after she confided in a Pentagon co-worker, Linda Tripp – who secretly recorded their conversations, which were then used in Paula Jones' sexual harassment lawsuit against Clinton – when the affair became public fodder.

During a January 1998 White House news conference, Clinton famously denied the affair, and stated, "I did not have sexual relations with that woman, Miss Lewinsky," and Lewinsky subsequently went into hiding due to public humiliation.
Bill Clinton was impeached while serving as the 42nd president. (House Judiciary Committee/Getty Images)

The subsequent impeachment trial against the 42nd president began in January 1999 and ended Feb. 12. While Clinton was impeached by the house, he was acquitted of perjury and obstruction of justice charges.
While the scandal made headlines for years, Lewinsky only truly began reclaiming her identity in the last decade.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"I feel really grateful. I'm really grateful, and I'm excited," she said. "It's when I step away, and I look at my own story objectively – or as objectively as one can – it is pretty extraordinary to still be here, like physically still here, and to have been able to help shape how people see me more and understand me more and connect with me in ways that are meaningful. It's bonkers."
Monica Lewinsky previously recalled the toll of receiving negative energy from "billions of strangers" over the years. (Robin L. Marshall)
Themes surrounding authority and control have remained a constant in Lewinsky's life post scandal.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"I think of power in two different ways. There's the power that someone has and they use, that impacts other people's power," Lewinsky explained to Fox News Digital earlier this year.
"Then there's the power that someone has in connection to themselves and that's a lot more like strength."

She added, "People often think of resilience as being linear, and it is so much more like a spiral. You will move forward, you'll go back, and move forward ... you'll go back, and I think it's, again, people have to be patient with themselves."
Tracy Wright is an entertainment reporter for Fox News Digital. Send story tips to Tracy.Wright@fox.com.

title: Ryan Gosling's family-first philosophy reshaped his Hollywood career: experts
summary: From "Barbie" to "Ghost Rider," Ryan Gosling's pivot toward blockbuster franchises traces back to a deliberate family-first philosophy he embraced as a dad.
story: Ryan Gosling and Sandra Hüller on epic adventure, science included, theme of being brave with challenging projects and how Goslings space wardrobe is a "love letter" to the late Val Kilmer in "Real Genius"
Ryan Gosling is officially joining the Marvel Cinematic Universe as Ghost Rider, marking the latest chapter in a career evolution that the actor has linked directly to fatherhood.

Earlier this month, Gosling, 45, made a surprise appearance during Marvel Studios' panel at San Diego Comic-Con where it was announced that he will be starring as the titular motorcycle-riding supernatural hero in a standalone "Ghost Rider" movie slated for release in 2028.

Gosling's casting comes as the three-time Oscar nominee continues to embrace blockbuster franchises after spending years building his reputation in some of Hollywood's darkest, most critically acclaimed dramas.
MARVEL STAR VINCENT D’ONOFRIO SAYS HE ‘CAN’T DO’ KINGPIN TRANSFORMATION ANYMORE
Ryan Gosling's family-first philosophy sparked his career evolution, according to experts. (Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images)

The actor has previously shared that his pivot toward lighter, more mainstream projects was intentional, explaining that his priorities changed after becoming a parent. Gosling shares daughters Esmeralda, 11, and Amada, 10, with his longtime partner, Eva Mendes, 52.
During a 2024 interview with The Wall Street Journal, Gosling said he avoids psychologically heavy roles because he wants to be emotionally present for Mendes and their daughters.

"I don’t really take roles that are going to put me in some kind of dark place," Gosling said. "This moment is what I feel like trying to read the room at home and feel like what is going to be best for all of us. The decisions I make, I make them with Eva, and we make them with our family in mind first."
‘DUCK DYNASTY’ STAR SADIE ROBERTSON HUFF ADMITS ‘FEARS’ OVER PUTTING HER KIDS ON REALITY TV
While speaking with Fox News Digital, PR expert Sarah Schmidt shared her view that Gosling's family-first approach has reshaped not only the types of roles he is taking, but the purpose behind them.
"He began picking lighter roles to keep his mood stable for his family and also create art that they can be a part of," the president of Interdependence PR said.
Gosling spent years building his reputation in critically acclaimed dramas before becoming a blockbuster leading man. (Lloyd Bishop/NBC via Getty Images)
Paul Dergarabedian, head of Marketplace Trends for Rentrak, said Gosling's evolving priorities reflect a broader pattern among actors whose careers change alongside their personal lives.

"It does feel as though he is gravitating toward movies that his kids could actually see and enjoy," Dergarabedian said. "That kind of evolution is not unique as we have seen it with other actors as they get older, start families, and begin making choices that reflect where they are in life, how they see the world, and how they want to be perceived both personally and professionally."

Gosling's shift toward family-friendly entertainment signals a full-circle career moment for the actor, who made his debut as a child performer on the Disney Channel's "The All-New Mickey Mouse Club." He later appeared in the children's TV shows "Are You Afraid of the Dark?" and "Goosebumps."

During a 2011 interview with The New York Times, Gosling recalled that he decided to pursue "serious acting" at age 19. After making his mainstream breakthrough in the hit 2004 romantic drama "The Notebook," the Canada native went on to establish himself as one of Hollywood's most respected dramatic actors with critically acclaimed films, including "Half Nelson," "Blue Valentine," "Drive," "The Place Beyond the Pines," "Blade Runner 2049" and "First Man."
Gosling shares daughters Esmeralda and Amada with his longtime partner, Eva Mendes, who he met on the set of "The Place Beyond the Pines." (Sonia Recchia/Getty Images)

In recent years, Gosling has charted a different course with starring roles in audience-friendly movies including "Barbie," "The Fall Guy," and "Project Hail Mary," and his upcoming turns in "Star Wars: Starfighter" and "Ghost Rider."
Ryan McCormick, co-founder of Goldman McCormick PR, said he believes Gosling has earned the creative freedom to balance blockbuster franchises with prestige films.

"Ryan has not only built a career of acclaimed roles, those films are often box office successes," McCormick told Fox News Digital. "He has attained a rare status where he can do a sandbox film like 'Ghost Rider' and also take a dramatic or independent role without any one performance limiting his future choices."
Dergarabedian noted that Gosling's career has long defied easy categorization, citing his performances in 2011's "Crazy, Stupid, Love" and 2016's "La La Land."
"Gosling has always been far more versatile than any single role would suggest," Dergarabedian said. "He has shown he can do comedy, as he did so memorably in ‘Crazy, Stupid, Love.'"
"Of course, he proved he could carry a musical with ‘La La Land,'" he added.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Gosling said that "La La Land" was the first project he chose because of his children. (Dale Robinette/Lionsgate)

Dergarabedian pointed to Gosling's starring role in Nicolas Winding Refn's "Drive" as a pivotal moment that expanded audiences' perception of him beyond romantic leads and demonstrated his ability to tackle darker, action-oriented material.

"You really cannot put Gosling in a box. He has been able to move between genres and tones with a level of ease that very few actors can match," Dergarabedian said. "All that being said, you can definitely see a shift in tone at this stage of his career."

Gosling previously shared that "La La Land" was the first project he chose that reflected his changing priorities after becoming a father. While speaking with The Wall Street Journal, Gosling recalled thinking of how Esmeralda and Amada would enjoy watching him prepare for the role.
"It was just sort of like, ‘Oh, this will be fun for them, too, because even though they’re not coming to set, we’re practicing piano every day, or we’re dancing, or we’re singing,'" Gosling said.
The philosophy carried over to 2023's "Barbie," which Gosling said resonated with his daughters, who were already immersed in the world of Barbie dolls before he signed on to play Ken.

"Their interest in Barbie and their disinterest in Ken was an inspiration," Gosling said. "I thought they were already making little movies about their Barbies on the iPad when it happened, so the fact that I was going off to work to make one too, we just felt like we were aligned."
The actor said his daughters inspired him to star in "Barbie." (Courtesy Warner Bros. Pictures)

Though some fans initially criticized Gosling's casting as Ken, arguing he was too old to portray Barbie's iconic counterpart, the actor ultimately won over audiences with a performance that became one of the film's biggest highlights. "Barbie" went on to gross more than $1.4 billion worldwide and Gosling earned an Oscar nomination for best supporting actor, cementing the film as both a commercial and critical triumph.
Schmidt told Fox News Digital that she believes the film fundamentally changed the trajectory of Gosling's career.
"Gosling proved that just because he began his career as a critically acclaimed darling does not mean that he cannot also be an international franchise and blockbuster star," she said.

"'Barbie' paved the way," Schmidt continued. "Prior to that, Gosling was a serious actor who occasionally moonlighted in a rom-com. As it turns out, Ken can carry a billion-dollar movie. He was funny and self-aware, and it did not cost him any of his hard-earned credibility."

Gosling has continued to embrace projects that his daughters can share with him. While promoting "Project Hail Mary," he revealed that Esmeralda and Amada occasionally voiced his alien co-star Rocky during rehearsals and became some of the sci-fi adventure movie's earliest viewers.
Gosling said his daughters helped him by sometimes voicing Rocky when he was filming "Project Hail Mary." (Jonathan Olley © 2026 Amazon Content Services LLC. All Rights Reserved.)

"Sometimes when I was working, and I needed to sort of switch things up or whatever, my kids would come in, and I had an earpiece in my ear, and they would talk for Rocky, so I could talk to them as Rocky," Gosling told People in March.

"And there's some moments in the movie where I'm laughing or I'm just so charmed by him, which is like, it's actually my kids talking to me and helping me out," Gosling continued.
"They've seen many cuts of this film," he added of his daughters. "They've given me many notes."

Marvel's "Ghost Rider" marks the latest chapter in the blockbuster era that Gosling has spent years building. Gosling's role as Johnny Blaze/Ghost Rider in the superhero movie will also reunite him with director Shawn Levy after the two previously collaborated on "Star Wars: Starfighter," which hits theaters in May 2027.
"Wow, is this really happening?" Gosling told the crowd at Comic-Con after being unveiled as Ghost Rider by Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige.
"As you know, this is a character I’ve wanted to play for a very long time," he said.
Gosling is starring in Marvel's "Ghost Rider," which will be released in 2028. (Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Disney)
Schmidt told Fox News Digital that she believes Gosling has found a way to balance artistic credibility with commercial success without losing sight of the priorities that reshaped his career.
"He became a dad first, actor second," Schmidt said. "He is building a filmography legacy that his kids can be part of and proud of."

Meanwhile, Dergarabedian said he believes Gosling's recent choices have also cemented his place among Hollywood's biggest stars.

"He has become a go-to actor for huge, audience-friendly studio films and major franchises because he occupies such a unique position within the public eye," Dergarabedian said. "He has credibility, he has charm, he has range, and he has that elusive movie-star quality that is increasingly rare today."
Ashley Hume is an entertainment journalist for Fox News Digital and Fox Business who covers breaking news, celebrity culture, major industry events and the business of entertainment.

title: Kate Middleton is 'indispensable' to royal family as slimmed-down monarchy faces mounting pressure: expert
summary: Royal expert Katie Nicholl calls Kate Middleton "the monarchy's greatest asset," revealing how her cancer journey forged a deeper bond with King Charles.
story: Katie Nicholl, Vanity Fair royal correspondent and co-host of "The Royals Uncensored," says the Princess of Wales won public respect through duty and resilience after health challenges.
Kate Middleton has become one of King Charles' most beloved family members, with one royal expert calling her the "monarchy's greatest asset."

The claim came from Vanity Fair royal correspondent Katie Nicholl, co-host of "The Royals Uncensored." After more than 20 years covering the royal family on tours and engagements, Nicholl said she has spoken to countless palace insiders, many of whom are enchanted by the Princess of Wales.

"I think Catherine, the Princess of Wales, has always been a very valuable asset to the royal family," Nicholl told Fox News Digital. "She is the commoner who married into the royal family ... [She has made] a seamless transition into that unique world of royalty. It's not easy ... There's a huge amount of sacrifice that goes into being a member of the royal family."
PRINCE WILLIAM, KATE MIDDLETON FINALLY FEEL FREE TO SHOW AFFECTION IN PUBLIC: EXPERTS

King Charles III kisses Catherine, Princess of Wales, after the Requiem Mass for the Duchess of Kent at Westminster Cathedral in London on Sept. 16, 2025. Royal experts told Fox News Digital the touching moment reflects the increasingly close relationship the monarch shares with his daughter-in-law. (Jordan Pettitt - Pool/Getty Images)
"Catherine's had to give up a huge amount, and yet she does it all with a great deal of grace and dignity, always with a smile," Nicholl said. "So she is absolutely the monarchy's greatest asset."
Nicholl also noted that "the king adores her, and the queen adores her."

Catherine, Princess of Wales speaks with children during an official welcome at the Town Hall on the first day of her visit to Reggio Emilia on May 13, 2026, in Reggio Emilia, Italy. (UK Press via Getty Images)

Royal experts told Fox News Digital that Charles and Kate have forged an even deeper bond since both were diagnosed with cancer. Buckingham Palace announced the king's diagnosis in 2024. In December 2025, Charles shared the "good news" that his treatment would be scaled back in 2026.
WATCH: KATE MIDDLETON IS 'THE MONARCHY'S GREATEST ASSET: EXPERT'

Just weeks after the king's announcement, Kate revealed in March 2024 that she was undergoing treatment for an undisclosed form of cancer. She completed chemotherapy that September and announced in January 2025 that she was in remission.
British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital that the king, 77, had been greatly inspired by the Princess of Wales' strength.
Catherine, Princess of Wales, Princess Charlotte of Wales and King Charles III during Trooping the Colour on June 15, 2024, in London. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)

"King Charles sees enormous value in Princess Catherine," Chard said. "Not just as the wife of his heir, but as the cornerstone of the monarchy itself. He genuinely loves his 'darling' daughter-in-law. His face lights up when he is with her. They share similar interests, and they have shared a similar cancer journey, one that has created a deep bond and understanding that goes beyond duty."

King Charles III and Catherine, Princess of Wales, are seen here at the state banquet for German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and his wife, Elke Budenbender, at Windsor Castle in Windsor, England, on Dec. 3, 2025. (Aaron Chown - Pool/Getty Images)
Chard argued that it hasn't just been Charles who quickly realized that Kate represented the monarchy's future.
"The late queen saw it too," Chard said. "She recognized Catherine's superpowers early on — her ability to listen, find solutions and bring calm to difficult situations."
Queen Elizabeth II, England's longest-reigning monarch, died in 2022 at age 96. (Geoff Pugh)

"King Charles fundamentally views his time on the throne as stewardship," she said. "He sees himself as the caretaker of the institution and is acutely conscious of preparing the next generation. Collaborative preparation between the king and his heir is essential. Having Princess Catherine as the wife of his heir, Charles has struck gold."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Prince William, Prince of Wales, Catherine, Princess of Wales, Princess Charlotte, Prince George and Prince Louis watch an RAF flypast from the balcony of Buckingham Palace after attending Trooping the Colour 2026 on June 13, 2026, in London. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
Royal author Sally Bedell Smith previously told People magazine that Kate is "like the daughter he never had."
"He has always had a very strong bond with her," Smith told the outlet. "He shares with William an impulse to protect her. They are in this together, Kate and the king."

Kate Middleton and the former Prince Charles examine artwork produced on silk during a visit to the Dulwich Picture Gallery on March 15, 2012, in Dulwich, south London, England. (John Stillwell - WPA Pool/Getty Images)
When Kate made her diagnosis public, Buckingham Palace said Charles was "so proud of Catherine for her courage in speaking as he did."

Catherine, Princess of Wales congratulates patient Claire Lorente and her partner, Pablo, as she rings the end-of-treatment bell at the Christie cancer care hospital in Manchester, England, on June 4, 2026. (Andy Stenning - WPA Pool/Getty Images)
Author Christopher Andersen previously wrote in his book "Kate!" that the king was by Kate's side "to lend his cherished daughter-in-law moral support" during her health battle.
Kate's advocacy work following her cancer diagnosis continues, Nicholl told Fox News Digital.
Catherine, Princess of Wales curtseys to King Charles III on Sept. 16, 2025, in London. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"Thankfully, despite a serious health issue, she has overcome that," Nicholl said. "We've just seen her climb the three highest peaks in the United Kingdom to raise money for the Royal Marsden. She's turning her experience into something positive, and I think that's earned her a great deal of respect among the British public, along with a lot of love and affection. People are very much behind her and William."
LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Catherine, Princess of Wales, is seen visiting Evelina London Children's Hospital in London, on July 6, 2026. (Anadolu via Getty Images)
Chard echoed those sentiments.

"Princess Catherine connects with people in a way that restores faith in the monarchy," Chard said. "She has learned every aspect of the institution over many years and has blended in carefully without fuss. Princess Catherine is central to the institution's success, and King Charles knows this."

With a slimmed down monarchy, Charles needs key allies now more than ever. His younger brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, stepped back as a working royal in 2019 following his controversial ties to late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Charles has since formally removed Andrew’s princely title and HRH style.

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested on Feb. 19, 2026, and released after about 11 hours under investigation. He was detained on suspicion of misconduct in public office over allegations that he shared confidential trade reports with Jeffrey Epstein while serving as the U.K.'s trade envoy. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
In 2020, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, stepped back as senior working royals and later settled in California.

From left: Prince William, Kate Middleton, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle attend a ceremony to mark the centenary of the Royal Air Force on the forecourt of Buckingham Palace on July 10, 2018, in London. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex stepped back as senior royals in 2020. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"Princess Anne and other senior working royals are all stretched thin — and none of them are young," author Catherine Mayer previously told People magazine. "William and Catherine carry the whole thing."
Sources told the outlet there had been "even greater attention and expectation on the Waleses." Still, royal experts told Fox News Digital that Kate is well-positioned to support the king.
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP
Queen Camilla, Prince William, King Charles and Kate Middleton are seen at the "No Time To Die" world premiere at the Royal Albert Hall in London, on Sept. 28, 2021. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)

"Naturally, King Charles recognizes the value of Kate, who is indeed the monarchy's greatest asset," Richard Fitzwilliams told Fox News Digital. "We should add, 'together with her partnership with William and their family.' While we praise Catherine's many strengths, William is the future king. She will one day be queen consort. They see themselves as a close-knit couple."

"William is currently at the center of reports that he and the king differ over how to handle Prince Harry, in particular," Fitzwilliams said. "As she showed when the Sussexes met with the king and Queen Camilla, she fully supports William's approach."

Catherine, Princess of Wales, speaks to guests during a Cancer Research UK reception marking the charity's 125th anniversary at St. James's Palace on June 2, 2026, in London. (Jonathan Brady - Pool/Getty Images)

As William and Kate prepare for their future roles, they are likely to remain under close public scrutiny. With Charles' support, royal experts believe the couple is well-positioned for the years ahead.
Prince William is heir to the British throne. (Aaron Chown - Pool/Getty Images)

"It’s not at all surprising King Charles and Princess Catherine have bonded," British royals expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital. "One can tangibly feel the public also values her wonderful assets from the reception she always receives when in public, as well as in opinion polls. She has become indispensable and has won the public’s trust."

"Charles can depend on Catherine because she is consistent, steady and modern in her approach to family, shaped by her upbringing and dedication to duty," Fordwich said. "She handled the strain of her cancer battle with dignity, without any indication of self-pity."

Catherine, Princess of Wales cools down with a fan as she attends Day 14 of the 2026 Wimbledon Tennis Championships at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club on July 12, 2026, in London. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)
"One can observe from the body language between Charles and Catherine that they are so comfortable together, derived from the time they spent together during their cancer battles."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Jessica Simpson celebrates turning 46 in bikini and reveals her children have never seen her perform
summary: Jessica Simpson shared a bikini selfie while tanning on her 46th birthday, staying true to her self-described identity as a lifelong "sun lover."
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Jessica Simpson celebrated 46 exactly how a self-described "sun lover" would.

Simpson reclined beneath a purple crocheted cover while wearing oval dark sunglasses. Her blonde hair was styled in a loose side braid, and she accessorized the polka-dot bikini with layered turquoise bead necklaces, a square green pendant, dangling stone earrings and stacked bracelets.

Jessica Simpson marked her 46th birthday with a bikini selfie while celebrating another trip around the sun. (Jessica Simpson/Instagram)

The birthday post comes as Simpson continues her return to music after years away from the stage.

title: America hits major marijuana milestone as daily weed use surpasses daily drinking
summary: Daily marijuana use among American adults jumped 21% between 2022 and 2025, with adults aged 26 and older driving the dramatic surge in cannabis use.
story: New research raises concerns about high-potency cannabis, as Fox News senior medical contributor Dr. Marc Siegel explains. Siegel highlights how increased THC levels contribute to addiction and adverse mental health effects, particularly in developing brains. He emphasizes that claims of cannabis helping with anxiety and depression are often bogus, leading to increased ER visits.
Marijuana is officially leading the pack for the most-used daily drug among Americans.

New data from the 2025 National Survey on Drug Use and Health, from the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), reveals that there are 21.4 million daily or near-daily marijuana users in the U.S.
This surpasses the 19.9 million people who smoke cigarettes and the 17.2 million who consume alcohol.
IS DRINKING EVERY DAY ALCOHOLISM? EXPERTS EXPLAIN WHERE CULTURE AND ADDICTION COLLIDE

The annual federal survey of Americans age 12 and older defines daily or near-daily use as consuming marijuana on 300 or more days in the past year. Daily cigarette smokers were characterized as those who smoked on all 30 days of the past month.
The number of Americans using marijuana daily or almost daily rose about 21% between 2022 and 2025. (iStock)

The number of Americans using marijuana daily or almost daily rose about 21% between 2022 and 2025 — from 17.7 million to approximately 21.4 million. This amounts to an increase of about 3.7 million frequent users.
The biggest jump occurred between 2021 and 2022 with an increase of roughly 2.8 million users, according to SAMSHA.
This pattern in higher marijuana use is driven mostly by adults, particularly those age 26 and older, rather than teenagers.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Between 2021 and 2025, the number of adults 18 and older using marijuana daily or almost daily increased about 22%, from 17.2 million to 20.9 million.

Although marijuana is now the most commonly used substance on a daily or near-daily basis, alcohol remains the most widely used substance overall. During the previous month, about 129 million people drank alcohol while 43.8 million used marijuana.
General marijuana use rose from 13.2% to 15.1% from 2021 to 2025. (iStock)

Cigarette and broader tobacco product use has been on a decline, decreasing from 20.1% of Americans in 2021 to 15.9% in 2025. Meanwhile, general marijuana use rose from 13.2% to 15.1% during that same period.

A recent report by San Francisco-based workplace mental health platform Modern Health found a concerning increase in the number of workers turning to substances to manage stress, especially THC and marijuana products.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The survey of 1,000 full-time employees in April 2026 found that 63% of the workforce engages in at least one form of self-medication after the workday, while 52% have self-medicated during the workday.

Gen Z is the only generation of workers where THC use exceeded alcohol use after work – 59% report using marijuana products compared to 50% who drink alcohol. In that group, 51% reported using THC during the workday.
A survey of 1,000 full-time employees in April 2026 found that 63% of the workforce engages in at least one form of self-medication after the workday. (iStock)
Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel said the SAMHSA data reflects a "very disturbing trend."

"Too much attention has been put on the bogus or exaggerated uses of marijuana for pain, insomnia and anxiety, when in fact it increases anxiety exponentially, especially in those with underlying mental health issues," he told Fox News Digital.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Too little attention has been paid to the growing THC content in all cannabis products, which makes it far more dangerous in terms of mental performance, judgement, memory and all forms of impairment."
THC has been associated with a growing share of fatal motor vehicle crashes, Siegel said, arguing that increased acceptance of marijuana use is "feeding a dangerous trend."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"So I firmly believe that the rising use – coupled with decreasing alcohol and cigarettes – is directly due to lack of awareness of all the dangers of marijuana versus an increased awareness of all the dangers of cigarettes and alcohol," he added.
Angelica Stabile is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: How often are married people having sex? What to know about the intimacy standard in America
summary: Research reveals once a week may be the sweet spot for marital satisfaction, with no added happiness boost from more frequent sexual intimacy.
story: Fox News Senior Medical Analyst Dr. Marc Siegel discusses the alarming decline in the U.S. fertility rate to a record low of 1.56 children per couple, highlighting impacts on population size. Dr. Siegel then explains the surge in seasonal allergies nationwide due to a cold winter and wet spring, emphasizing the "hygiene hypothesis" in immune system development.
New survey data offers a snapshot of how often married Americans are having sex, while researchers say the findings challenge common assumptions about relationship health.

National demographic studies suggest that lower sexual frequency is often a normal part of aging and long-term relationships, and that there may be a "sweet spot" associated with marital satisfaction.
Data from the General Social Survey, conducted by NORC at the University of Chicago, found that married Americans report a wide range of sexual frequency.
WEIGHT-LOSS MEDICATIONS COULD IMPACT SEXUAL HEALTH IN UNEXPECTED WAYS
The survey asked how often couples have had sex during the last 12 months. Among the 1,893 married respondents surveyed in 2024, the responses were as follows.
New survey data offers a snapshot of how often married Americans are having sex, while researchers say the findings challenge common assumptions about relationship health. (iStock)

32.5% said not at all11.3% said once or twice during the year11.7% said about once a month15.3% said two or three times a month12.9% said about once a week12.2% said two or three times a week4.1% said more than three times a week
32.5% said not at all
11.3% said once or twice during the year
11.7% said about once a month
15.3% said two or three times a month
12.9% said about once a week
12.2% said two or three times a week
4.1% said more than three times a week
The average American adult has sex 53 times a year — or a little more than once per week, according to research by the telehealth platform Hims.
The average American adult has sex 53 times a year — or a little more than once per week, according to research by the telehealth platform Hims. (iStock)

While marriage is often associated with less frequent sex, research has found the difference to be relatively small. A 2014 study found that married people had sex about 55 times a year, compared with 59 times a year among their unmarried peers.
"There’s no ‘perfect statistic’ or ideal amount of sex."

"Experts aren’t sure precisely why this difference exists or why what used to be an advantage has become a disadvantage, but some believe it may be related to the increasing age at which most people get married," Hims wrote in a medically reviewed article.
"There’s no ‘perfect statistic’ or ideal amount of sex. In other words: You like what you like, and that’s perfectly OK."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Clinical data suggests that aiming for a daily or high-volume sexual quota does not actually improve relationship quality.
A study published in Social Psychological and Personality Science in 2015 evaluated more than 30,000 individuals over four decades and discovered a drop-off in additional benefits.
Roughly 17% of adults aged 70 and older engage in sexual activity on a weekly basis, according to AARP data. (iStock)

While overall happiness increased as physical intimacy moved from monthly to weekly, couples who had sex two, three or four times a week experienced no additional statistical boost in marital satisfaction compared to those hitting the weekly threshold.
Experts emphasize that sexual desire naturally fluctuates as couples navigate career demands, parenthood and biological aging.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Despite some research suggesting a slowdown with age, intimacy remains an important factor in healthy aging, linked to improved physical and emotional well-being.
AARP survey data indicates that physical connection remains routine for many older Americans, with roughly 17% of adults aged 70 and older engaging in sexual activity on a weekly basis.
Reasons for declining intimacy
When a couple experiences an intimacy dry spell, medical professionals recommend evaluating physiological factors rather than jumping to conclusions about incompatibility.
Healthcare providers encourage couples dealing with mismatched sexual desire to discuss the issue openly and consult a doctor. (iStock)
Educational resources from the International Society for Sexual Medicine note that the following physical conditions can influence libido.

Rather than trying to force a weekly goal, healthcare providers encourage couples dealing with mismatched sexual desire to discuss the issue openly and consult a doctor to evaluate baseline hormone levels, medication profiles and overall metabolic health.
