Authorities said about 240 homes have been destroyed, while nearly 4,000 holidaymakers have been evacuated from campsites, holiday villages and tourist resorts in Lacanau, about 35 miles west of Bordeaux.
As France and Spain battle one of Europe's worst wildfire seasons in decades, roughly 360,000 people have been forced to evacuate in recent days.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: Japan mall rebuilt after deadly 2016 earthquake destroyed in major temblor weeks after 'fresh start' reopening
summary: A massive explosion ripped through Aeon Mall in Kumamoto just weeks after its grand reopening, leaving up to 30 employees unaccounted for.
story: Video from a surveillance camera shows stationary trucks shaking after an earthquake hit Kumamoto, Japan. (Credit: Reuters)

A shopping mall in southern Japan that had just reopened after years of reconstruction following a devastating 2016 earthquake was destroyed Tuesday after a powerful earthquake struck the region and was followed by a massive explosion, leaving dozens of workers unaccounted for.
The Aeon Mall in Kumamoto Prefecture celebrated its grand reopening on June 13 after years of rebuilding meant to mark the region's recovery from the 2016 disaster.

Just weeks later, a magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck near Kumamoto, according to FOX Weather, citing the U.S. Geological Survey. Japan's Meteorological Agency measured the same quake at magnitude 7.1 using its own seismic scale.
EARTHQUAKE SHAKES PERU'S ANDES REGION, KILLING AT LEAST 5, DISPLACING HUNDREDS

An aerial view shows a collapsed chimney at Nippon Paper Industries' Yatsushiro Mill after an earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.1 struck Japan's southern Kumamoto prefecture, in Yatsushiro, July 28, 2026. (yodo/via Reuters/TPX Images of the Day)

About 200 shoppers were safely evacuated after the earthquake, officials said. Roughly an hour later, a powerful explosion ripped through the building, blowing off exterior walls and exposing its steel framework. NHK reported that about 20 to 30 mall employees remained unaccounted for, while police said rescuers could not immediately enter because of the risk of aftershocks.

The mall had become one of the most visible symbols of Kumamoto's recovery after the magnitude 7.3 earthquake that devastated the region in April 2016. Aeon said the redevelopment included seismic reinforcements and other safety improvements designed to make the complex more resilient.

Witnesses reported smelling gas before the explosion, according to Reuters. An Aeon spokesperson said employees immediately helped evacuate visitors after the quake, while prefectural officials confirmed about 200 people were guided safely outside before the blast.
EXCLUSIVE: FRANKLIN GRAHAM VISITS EMERGENCY HOSPITAL TREATING VENEZUELA EARTHQUAKE VICTIMS

The damaged Aeon Mall shopping centre, where, according to local media, an explosion occurred after an earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.1 struck Japan's southern Kumamoto Prefecture, in Kashima Town, July 28, 2026.  (Kyodo/via Reuters)

According to FOX Weather, the earthquake struck just before 4:30 p.m. local time about 9 miles north of Kumamoto at a depth of roughly 6 miles. Japan's Meteorological Agency briefly issued and later lifted a tsunami advisory for parts of Kyushu. NHK reported at least 50 people were injured, while Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency said the quake sparked at least eight fires. Kumamoto Airport also temporarily closed.
Reuters reported the mall welcomed more than 8 million visitors annually after Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. opened a factory nearby in 2024.

The complex housed about 200 stores, a movie theater and parking for roughly 5,000 vehicles. It also became known locally after a supermarket inside sold 10-yen onigiri to help survivors following the 2016 earthquake.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Rescue workers conduct a search and rescue operation at the damaged Aeon Mall in Japan's southern Kumamoto prefecture, in Kashima Town, July 28, 2026. (Credit: Japan Out via Reuters)
When the mall reopened in June, Aeon described the project as a "'re-start' initiative" marking both the shopping center's 21st anniversary and the region's recovery from the 2016 earthquake.
As night fell Tuesday, rescue operations remained on hold because of continuing aftershocks as families awaited word on the employees still believed to be inside.
Jasmine Baehr is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital, where she covers politics, the military, legal debates surrounding life and family policy, as well as faith and culture.

title: U.S. agrees to pause attacks on Iran subject to ‘rapidly’ making deal, Trump says
summary: The U.S. has agreed to pause attacks on Iran, President Donald Trump said Saturday, amid what he said were the “perimeters of a deal” being agreed upon, which would include the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
story: The U.S. has agreed to pause attacks on Iran, President Donald Trump said Saturday, amid what he said were the “perimeters of a deal” being agreed upon, which would include the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

“We have just been asked by Iran, and other Middle Eastern Countries, to hold off any attack in that the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social. “This would include the Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran’s  nuclear threat.”
The president said the U.S. was “locked and loaded and ready to go” against Iran but that he agreed to cancel attacks “subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL.”
He added that Israel, the U.S. partner in the war with Iran, “joins me in this commitment.”
“Get to work, everybody, and get it DONE,” Trump said of a possible new agreement.

The statement came after the State Department on Saturday urged Americans across the Middle East to consider leaving the region or be prepared to depart on short notice. It also warned of flight disruptions and security risks as the conflict with Iran appeared to be escalating.

Trump earlier threatened Iran with additional attacks, saying Friday that the U.S. will be “hitting them very hard,” while Iran has vowed to “punish” the U.S. and both nations traded what some U.S. officials described as “heavy” strikes.
Responding to Trump’s announcement, Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) told “Meet the Press” Sunday that the president should not trust Iran’s word.
Asked why a fresh deal would be different when the Memorandum of Understanding signed in June failed, he told moderator Kristen Welker: “Well, it may not be.”
“We only have three choices: escalate, retreat and come home, or maintain the status quo. I would maintain the status quo as long as I could,” he said.
Iran’s acting minister of defense, Iran Majid Ibn al-Reza, meanwhile said that U.S. remarks should be viewed as “psychological and cognitive warfare.”
He said on X that the threat of further strikes would be taken “as the basis for increasing readiness, strengthening deterrence, and enhancing our own power.”

Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman, a key regional player, spoke with Trump by phone Saturday. According to the Saudi state news agency, he told him that dialogue was needed to de-escalate Middle East tensions, and expressed concerns over plans for new strikes against Iran.
The State Department issued fresh security guidance Saturday for Americans in the region.

“Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise caution and heightened vigilance and should be prepared for flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruptions,” the State Department said. “Some airlines in the region have postponed resumption of earlier flight schedules; others have cancelled some routes. Americans in the region should consider departing, or be prepared to depart should there be escalation.”
The State Department also urged Americans to reconsider travel bans to or through the region.
The warning was distributed through U.S. embassies in the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Iraq, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

The agency posted a nearly identical statement earlier this month, but that bulletin did not urge Americans to prepare to leave the Middle East or to reconsider upcoming trips, reflecting Washington’s growing concern that the conflict could widen.
On Saturday, the Kuwait Army said its air defense systems intercepted drone attacks from Iran.

“Kuwaiti air defenses are currently engaging hostile drone attacks following the Iranian aggression. The General Staff of the Army notes that any explosions heard are a result of air defense systems intercepting the hostile attacks,” the army said.

Two days ago, the U.S. military confirmed it had executed a “heavy wave of strikes” on Iran, hours after Fox News reported that the president in a phone call had vowed to “beat the f-----g s--- out of” the country.
Trump has grown increasingly exasperated with the state of the war, one Trump ally told NBC News.
“There was not a real strategy for how long or what they should do to get to the endpoint,” the ally said.
The conflict has now entered its sixth month, despite Trump’s repeated early predictions that the war would resolve itself “shortly.”
The protracted conflict has led to soaring oil prices globally and rising gas prices in the U.S.
There was a brief reprieve from fighting in June when the U.S. and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding outlining the process for talks to end the war.
But in early July, Trump declared a ceasefire to be “over” and the countries resumed striking targets in the Middle East.

title: Truth Social launches service selling faster access to Trump posts
summary: Wall Street firms can now be alerted of the “most market-moving” social media posts from President Donald Trump before the general public — as long as they pay the right price.
story: Wall Street firms can now be alerted of the “most market-moving” social media posts from President Donald Trump before the general public — as long as they pay the right price.

The service went live Saturday: a subscription to his social media platform, Truth Social, that allows financial firms and other organizations to get alerts for new posts made by Trump and other top accounts before general users do.

Trump Media and Technology Group, which owns the platform, launched the new high-speed data feed called “Truth API,” describing it as giving firms “a direct, licensed, real-time feed of the platform’s most market-moving Truths.”

Trump, who has the largest following on the platform by far with 13 million followers, has used Truth Social as his go-to platform to release official statements throughout his second term, including to announce that he was imposing sweeping new tariffs or to declare major military operations.

Trump’s unprecedented use of social media to reveal updates on global affairs and economic policy has contrasted sharply with prior presidents, who generally made such announcements through more formal avenues, such as through the White House press office and the official White House website.

Many trading firms already plug into Trump’s posts through Bloomberg, Reuters or other services that scrape his posts and relay them in real time to their customers. But using this data feed on Truth Social could enable firms to access his posts seconds or even milliseconds faster than the general public.
For a high-frequency trading firm, even milliseconds could make a huge difference.

The president also stands to profit from the new service. Trump is a major stakeholder in TMTG, owning 114.75 million shares to represent 41% of the company, according to his 2025 financial disclosure.

Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Adam Schiff, D-Calif., have urged the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to investigate whether Trump Media is violating the law by selling faster access to the president’s posts.

The senators wrote that the subscription “appears to be an outrageous abuse of the President’s office for his personal benefit that undermines everyday investors and the integrity of our markets, while enriching Wall Street and other wealthy insiders.”
In its announcement of the new service last month, TMTG emphasized Truth Social’s impact on the market.

“Markets already move on Truth Social posts,” Kevin McGurn, interim chief executive officer of TMTG, said in a press release. “Truth API delivers a direct, licensed, real-time feed of the platform’s most market-moving Truths while advancing our strategy to monetize proprietary assets through a high-margin, recurring revenue stream.”
Trump launched Truth Social in early 2022 after he had been banned from X, formerly known as Twitter, and other social media platforms in 2021 following the attacks on the Capitol on Jan. 6.
Elon Musk reinstated Trump’s access to X in November 2022 shortly after he took over the platform as CEO. Trump also regained access to Facebook and Instagram in January 2023.

title: Trump rebukes Jeanine Pirro over decision to drop Reflecting Pool vandalism case
summary: President Donald Trump criticized longtime ally Jeanine Pirro Saturday after she agreed to drop a case against a former Olympic canoeist who was accused of vandalizing the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.
story: President Donald Trump criticized longtime ally Jeanine Pirro Saturday after she agreed to drop a case against a former Olympic canoeist who was accused of vandalizing the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

“I disagree 100% with Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, on the Reflecting Pool. I don’t know what she was thinking?” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post, adding “it was a pure case of VANDALISM.”
“There may have been some contractor difficulty, but the major damage was caused by VANDALS!” the president added.

Pirro’s office, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia, said Friday it had obtained information that undermined “the evidentiary basis for the indictment” against David “Davey” Hearn.

Hearn was indicted on July 2 over claims that he was “forcefully and violently pulling up and removing the bottom liner” of the pool with both hands on June 19 — shortly after the pool had undergone renovations directed by the president.
Hearn pleaded not guilty and has said that “the condition of the Reflecting Pool was the same after I stepped away from the water as it was before I got there.”

Prosecutors said Friday that they received new information from the Interior Department after Hearn’s indictment that indicated that the damage to the pool “was the result of flawed installation by the contractor, Atlantic Industrial Coatings.”

Hearn was one of several people arrested in June after the pool was seen covered in green algae and pieces of its blue sealant had peeled away in several places, resulting in chunks of the material floating on the water’s surface.
Trump, who directed a $14 million-plus renovation project that included coating the pool in “American flag blue,” has repeatedly argued that the pool’s issues were caused by vandals.
In a second post Saturday, the president argued that surveillance video clearly showed vandalism at the pool.
“Look for yourselves at the VANDALISM that took place at The Reflecting Pool. The material is being cut with a knife or a box cutter, for all to see!” Trump wrote.
On Friday, the Justice Department said it “first became aware of information showing that the damage was the result of a botched installation and not vandalism” after reviewing more documents.
The DOJ said that it wouldn’t have sought a grand jury indictment against Hearn had it initially received the documents that the Interior Department provided after the indictment.
Interior Secretary Doug Burgum continued to stand by Trump’s claims of vandalism on Saturday, despite the findings presented by Pirro’s office.
“The evidence is clear, vandals have repeatedly caused damage to the Reflecting Pool. Some of these acts were even caught on camera,” Burgum wrote in a post on X.

Burgum wrote that his office “also provided the U.S. Attorney’s office expert and eyewitness testimony to the damage done by vandals and provided every piece of evidence they asked for in the requested time line detailing each area of damage at the pool.”
Hearn’s lawyer said in a statement Friday that the Trump administration owes Hearn an apology.

“The Government’s case against Davey Hearn should never have been brought,” Steven Levin, Hearn’s attorney, said in a statement. “Its dismissal today does not erase the abuse of government power in arresting and charging a patriotic American. The government’s approach was ready, shoot, aim. The federal government owes Mr. Hearn an apology.”
Pirro’s office said Friday that it also moved to dismiss at least one of the other three misdemeanor cases against those who allegedly vandalized the pool.

title: Trump says he’ll revive ‘anti-weaponization’ fund if Blanche’s nomination for AG is blocked
summary: Trump threatened to “push hard” to keep a $1.8 billion “anti-weaponization” fund active, amid an ongoing feud between two Republican senators and the Trump administration over Todd Blanche’s nomination for attorney general.
story: President Donald Trump on Saturday threatened to “push hard” to keep a $1.8 billion “anti-weaponization” fund active, amid an ongoing feud between two Republican senators and the Trump administration over the president’s nomination of Todd Blanche for attorney general.

“If Senators Cornyn and Tillis, both upset because I wouldn’t Endorse them (they lost, and quit, respectively!), aren’t going to approve Todd Blanche, one of the most respected professionals, according to everybody, in the Country, to be the United States Attorney General, then I will keep Todd as Acting A.G., and push hard to get the Anti-Weaponization Bill, which takes care of those who have been so badly treated by the Crooked Joe Biden (and Obuma!) Administration (I get nothing, although I was treated horribly!), PASSED,” the president wrote in a post on Truth Social.
“Todd Blanche was a voice of reason! It will immediately be back on the table, and I will get it done. Thank you for your attention to this matter!” he added.

Sens. John Cornyn, R-Texas, and Thom Tillis, R-N.C., are both departing Congress after feuding with Trump. In Texas, Cornyn ran for re-election, losing in a primary runoff to state Attorney General Ken Paxton after Trump endorsed Paxton.
Tillis, in North Carolina, opted not to run for re-election, making his plans to retire public one day after drawing Trump’s ire for opposing a GOP-backed domestic policy package.

The two senators have partially conditioned their support for Blanche’s nomination on the Trump administration rescinding its plans for the fund, which would provide compensation for Jan. 6 rioters pardoned by Trump for claims of government overreach.
In a post on X following Trump’s statement Saturday, Tillis blamed the president for Blanche’s stalled confirmation.

“Despite comments as late as yesterday that the fund is dead, President Trump clearly intends to resurrect the payout pot for punks either by inappropriately establishing another bogus fund or pushing Congress to vote for a bill that the majority of Republicans in the Senate would be against,” he wrote.
“It’s unfortunate that Todd Blanche, who I consider qualified for the job, will not be confirmed because of this reversal. Hopefully, we can resolve this by Tuesday,” Tillis added.

Blanche’s nomination has been in jeopardy for several weeks, with Cornyn and Tillis previously saying that there are other Republican senators that share their concerns but don’t sit on the Judiciary Committee and wouldn’t have the chance to vote for or against Blanche until his nomination came to the floor.
On Wednesday night, the committee postponed a vote on Blanche’s nomination because of Cornyn and Tillis’ concerns.
On Friday, at a Cabinet meeting, the president defended the fund, saying, “It is dead, but you know, I wish it weren’t.”
“This has nothing to do with Todd,” Trump added.
The anti-weaponization fund has been blocked indefinitely by a federal judge, but the Trump administration has not pledged to stop pursuing it.

The fund was part of a settlement agreement that stemmed from a lawsuit Trump filed against the IRS. Also part of that settlement was an agreement that made the president and several family members immune from IRS audits, another provision that Cornyn and Tillis have shared concerns about.
Earlier this week, the president threatened to withdraw Blanche’s nomination and resubmit it next year, after Tillis and Cornyn have left office.

“Hey, in 158 days they can try it again, roll the dice on what the Senate confirmation process looks like next year,” Tillis told reporters at the Capitol after that threat. “It’s all on him. Certainly within his authority to do that.”

title: At least 3 killed in Idaho In-N-Out Burger shooting; suspect dead
summary: Three people are dead in a shooting around an In-N-Out Burger in Twin Falls, Idaho, on Saturday, authorities said.
story: Three people are dead in a shooting around an In-N-Out Burger in Twin Falls, Idaho, on Saturday, authorities said.
At least five people were injured in the violence, Twin Falls Police Department said.
Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said a suspected shooter has died. It was not clear whether the shooter was being counted among the three dead.
The identity of the suspect and a possible motive were part of the investigation, Hicks said.
“We believe the threat to the community is over,” he said at a news conference. “The suspected shooter in this incident is deceased.”
Lynsi Snyder, President of In-N-Out Burger, said a worker was among those killed.

“She was taking care of our most important asset — our customers, and her life was taken by a disgusting human who doesn’t value the lives of others or his own,” Snyder said. She added: “He shot both on our property and off, and ended his life shortly after he took the precious lives of our associate and customers, innocent people who never saw it coming.”
City, county and state authorities responded to reports of an active shooter in the area of an In-N-Out on Blue Lakes Boulevard North around 2:30 p.m., police said.
The area is also the location of multiple major retailers and a movie theater complex. Hicks said hundreds of potential witnesses were expected to be interviewed.
“Today has been a very hard day here in Twin Falls,” he said.
A shelter-in-place order for the area was later lifted and roads were being reopened as the shooting investigation continued, Palmer said.
A nearby Chick-fil-A said it was closing Saturday as a precaution.
“Out of an abundance of caution, Chick-fil-A Twin Falls will be closed for the remainder of today,” the restaurant said.
Magic Valley Mall nearby was closed and people inside were told to stay put, a public safety employee there said earlier Saturday afternoon.
The In-N-Out location, the fourth in Idaho, opened July 24, according to a news release from the California-based chain.

title: Vincent Pastore, mob enforcer on ‘The Sopranos,’ dies at 80
summary: Vincent Pastore, who played Tony Soprano’s best friend turned informant on HBO’s mob drama “The Sopranos,” has died, a representative confirmed Saturday.
story: Vincent Pastore, who played Tony Soprano’s best friend turned informant on HBO’s mob drama “The Sopranos,” has died, a representative confirmed Saturday.
He was 80.
Manager Robert Attermann said Pastore, a longtime resident of the Bronx borough of New York City, died at home. He confirmed  that friends found his body Saturday.
A cause of death was not provided.

“To the world, he will always be remembered as the unforgettable ‘Big Pussy,’” he said, using the nickname of Pastore’s “Sopranos” character, Salvatore Bonpensiero, “but to those of us who knew him, he was so much more.”

A longtime actor who plied his trade within the sordid and violent  narratives of the Italian American mob, Pastore became a household face in 1999 when he was cast cast as Bonpensiero, mob boss Tony Soprano’s best friend, a family enforcer and ultimately an FBI informant who threatened to upend the New Jersey mob’s enterprise on the acclaimed drama.
He was born in the Bronx, grew up in New Rochelle, New York, served in the U.S. Navy, and attended Pace University, according to an IMDb biography.

He has said he worked in the nightclub industry. But he also tried acting, and after befriending Matt Dillon and Kevin Dillon he decided to dive in, he said during a 2015 appearance on “Good Day New York.”
According to his bio at the website for HB Studio, where he was an instructor, one of Pastore’s breakthroughs as an actor was in director Nancy Savoca’s Bronx comedy “True Love.”

He also appeared on television’s “Law & Order” and as an extra in director Martin Scorsese’s 1990 mob classic “Goodfellas.” He appeared in a string of mob narratives on New York City stages and on the big screen.
Pastore became a staple in films and television dramas about organized crime, including a role in “Once Upon a Time in Brooklyn.” But it was “The Sopranos’” six-season run that made him a true star.

“His portrayal of the complex and lovable mobster earned him widespread recognition and praise,” said the Bronx Walk of Fame, which inducted the actor in 2016. “Pastore’s ability to bring depth and authenticity to his character contributed to the show’s success and solidified his place in television history.”
The character’s nickname, Big Pussy, is rumored to have originated during his time as a cat burglar. It distinguished him from another character, Little Pussy Malanga.

The actor also had a musical side and performed with bands, including fronting Gangster Squad, a band familiar to small venues in New York, New Jersey and Connecticut. The band’s Facebook group says it specialized in “a mixture of classic hits from all different music genres, Rhythm and Blues, Rock & Roll, Funk, Soul, and Reggae.”
One of his most difficult gigs in the entertainment industry was during his brief 2007 stint on television’s “Dancing With the Stars,” where he lasted one week.
He said at the time that the training was too difficult.

Pastore founded Renegade Theater NYC with fellow “Sopranos” actor Maureen Van Zandt, wife of Steven Van Zandt, according to HB Studio. His Renegade Theater bio says he wrote “Crazy Horse,” describing it as “a hit play based on the story of his life as a Rock and Roll club owner.”
Musician and “Sopranos” castmate Steven Van Zandt memorialized Pastore on social media, calling him “another irreplaceable brother” who has died.
“It never gets any easier,” he said. “Travel well Vincenzo.”
Speaking on Instagram, “Sopranos” costar Michael Imperioli​ reminisced about traveling with Pastore in the United States, Italy, and Australia.
“Lots of good times,” he said. “Lots of laughs. Vinny was a kind hearted brother who cared deeply about his family and friends. I will miss him always.”
Lorraine Bracco, who played Tony Soprano’s psychiatrist on the HBO drama, said on the same platform that Pastore was “a beautiful soul.”
“Absolutely heartbreaking,” she said.
Attermann said he represented Pastore for more than 30 years — long before his HBO fame.

“Vinny was one of the kindest, most generous people I have ever known,” he said. “He treated everyone with warmth and respect, never turning down a fan who wanted a photograph or an autograph. He genuinely appreciated the people who supported him and always made them feel valued.”
Pastore “loved being an actor” and encouraging others interested in the craft, Atterman said.
He added, “I will miss his friendship, his loyalty, his humor, and his generosity. ... May his memory be a blessing.”

On Friday, the Justice Department said it “first became aware of information showing that the damage was the result of a botched installation and not vandalism” after reviewing more documents.
The DOJ said that it wouldn’t have sought a grand jury indictment against Hearn had it initially received the documents that the Interior Department provided after the indictment.
Interior Secretary Doug Burgum continued to stand by Trump’s claims of vandalism on Saturday, despite the findings presented by Pirro’s office.
“The evidence is clear, vandals have repeatedly caused damage to the Reflecting Pool. Some of these acts were even caught on camera,” Burgum wrote in a post on X.

Burgum wrote that his office “also provided the U.S. Attorney’s office expert and eyewitness testimony to the damage done by vandals and provided every piece of evidence they asked for in the requested time line detailing each area of damage at the pool.”
Hearn’s lawyer said in a statement Friday that the Trump administration owes Hearn an apology.

“The Government’s case against Davey Hearn should never have been brought,” Steven Levin, Hearn’s attorney, said in a statement. “Its dismissal today does not erase the abuse of government power in arresting and charging a patriotic American. The government’s approach was ready, shoot, aim. The federal government owes Mr. Hearn an apology.”
Pirro’s office said Friday that it also moved to dismiss at least one of the other three misdemeanor cases against those who allegedly vandalized the pool.

title: U.S. agrees to pause attacks on Iran subject to ‘rapidly’ making deal, Trump says
summary: The U.S. has agreed to pause attacks on Iran, President Donald Trump said Saturday, amid what he said were the “perimeters of a deal” being agreed upon, which would include the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
story: The U.S. has agreed to pause attacks on Iran, President Donald Trump said Saturday, amid what he said were the “perimeters of a deal” being agreed upon, which would include the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

“We have just been asked by Iran, and other Middle Eastern Countries, to hold off any attack in that the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social. “This would include the Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran’s  nuclear threat.”
The president said the U.S. was “locked and loaded and ready to go” against Iran but that he agreed to cancel attacks “subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL.”
He added that Israel, the U.S. partner in the war with Iran, “joins me in this commitment.”
“Get to work, everybody, and get it DONE,” Trump said of a possible new agreement.

The statement came after the State Department on Saturday urged Americans across the Middle East to consider leaving the region or be prepared to depart on short notice. It also warned of flight disruptions and security risks as the conflict with Iran appeared to be escalating.

Trump earlier threatened Iran with additional attacks, saying Friday that the U.S. will be “hitting them very hard,” while Iran has vowed to “punish” the U.S. and both nations traded what some U.S. officials described as “heavy” strikes.
Responding to Trump’s announcement, Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) told “Meet the Press” Sunday that the president should not trust Iran’s word.
Asked why a fresh deal would be different when the Memorandum of Understanding signed in June failed, he told moderator Kristen Welker: “Well, it may not be.”
“We only have three choices: escalate, retreat and come home, or maintain the status quo. I would maintain the status quo as long as I could,” he said.
Iran’s acting minister of defense, Iran Majid Ibn al-Reza, meanwhile said that U.S. remarks should be viewed as “psychological and cognitive warfare.”
He said on X that the threat of further strikes would be taken “as the basis for increasing readiness, strengthening deterrence, and enhancing our own power.”

Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman, a key regional player, spoke with Trump by phone Saturday. According to the Saudi state news agency, he told him that dialogue was needed to de-escalate Middle East tensions, and expressed concerns over plans for new strikes against Iran.
The State Department issued fresh security guidance Saturday for Americans in the region.

“Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise caution and heightened vigilance and should be prepared for flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruptions,” the State Department said. “Some airlines in the region have postponed resumption of earlier flight schedules; others have cancelled some routes. Americans in the region should consider departing, or be prepared to depart should there be escalation.”
The State Department also urged Americans to reconsider travel bans to or through the region.
The warning was distributed through U.S. embassies in the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Iraq, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

The agency posted a nearly identical statement earlier this month, but that bulletin did not urge Americans to prepare to leave the Middle East or to reconsider upcoming trips, reflecting Washington’s growing concern that the conflict could widen.
On Saturday, the Kuwait Army said its air defense systems intercepted drone attacks from Iran.

“Kuwaiti air defenses are currently engaging hostile drone attacks following the Iranian aggression. The General Staff of the Army notes that any explosions heard are a result of air defense systems intercepting the hostile attacks,” the army said.

Two days ago, the U.S. military confirmed it had executed a “heavy wave of strikes” on Iran, hours after Fox News reported that the president in a phone call had vowed to “beat the f-----g s--- out of” the country.
Trump has grown increasingly exasperated with the state of the war, one Trump ally told NBC News.
“There was not a real strategy for how long or what they should do to get to the endpoint,” the ally said.
The conflict has now entered its sixth month, despite Trump’s repeated early predictions that the war would resolve itself “shortly.”
The protracted conflict has led to soaring oil prices globally and rising gas prices in the U.S.
There was a brief reprieve from fighting in June when the U.S. and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding outlining the process for talks to end the war.
But in early July, Trump declared a ceasefire to be “over” and the countries resumed striking targets in the Middle East.

title: Troy Jackson launches first general election ad in Maine Senate race
summary: Maine’s Democratic Senate nominee Troy Jackson is launching his first general election ad, highlighting his own background as a labor organizer and going after Republican Sen.
story: Maine’s Democratic Senate nominee Troy Jackson is launching his first general election ad, highlighting his own background as a labor organizer and going after Republican Sen. Susan Collins.
The 30-second spot, narrated by Jackson, is backed by a seven-figure buy slated to begin airing statewide next week, his campaign told NBC News on Saturday.

“I’m a fifth-generation logger and the son of a public school teacher. My dad would work 16-hour days, and that still wasn’t enough. So when they tried to replace us with foreign labor, I led a blockade of the border,” Jackson says in the ad. “Susan Collins didn’t help us then, and she’s certainly not helping us now. We’re all getting crushed out here. Healthcare, housing, heat.”
“We’ve gotta fight back. We’re all hungry for it. Maine is ready for a change,” Jackson concludes.
The new ad points to Jackson’s strategy against Collins: paint her as a part of an establishment that is failing struggling Mainers.

It comes one week after Jackson accepted his party’s nomination for the seat at a convention in Bangor, replacing Graham Platner, who won the June primary but dropped out after a former girlfriend’s allegation of sexual assault, which he denied.

Collins, who was first elected in 1996, is running for a sixth term. She is campaigning as a moderate who brings money home to Maine, pointing to her chairmanship of the Appropriations Committee, and as someone who’s sometimes willing to break with President Donald Trump and her party’s leaders.
Maine, a blue-leaning state, represents one of the best pickup opportunities for Democrats, who need a net gain of four seats to capture control of the Senate.

title: Trump says he’ll revive ‘anti-weaponization’ fund if Blanche’s nomination for AG is blocked
summary: Trump threatened to “push hard” to keep a $1.8 billion “anti-weaponization” fund active, amid an ongoing feud between two Republican senators and the Trump administration over Todd Blanche’s nomination for attorney general.
story: President Donald Trump on Saturday threatened to “push hard” to keep a $1.8 billion “anti-weaponization” fund active, amid an ongoing feud between two Republican senators and the Trump administration over the president’s nomination of Todd Blanche for attorney general.

“If Senators Cornyn and Tillis, both upset because I wouldn’t Endorse them (they lost, and quit, respectively!), aren’t going to approve Todd Blanche, one of the most respected professionals, according to everybody, in the Country, to be the United States Attorney General, then I will keep Todd as Acting A.G., and push hard to get the Anti-Weaponization Bill, which takes care of those who have been so badly treated by the Crooked Joe Biden (and Obuma!) Administration (I get nothing, although I was treated horribly!), PASSED,” the president wrote in a post on Truth Social.
“Todd Blanche was a voice of reason! It will immediately be back on the table, and I will get it done. Thank you for your attention to this matter!” he added.

Sens. John Cornyn, R-Texas, and Thom Tillis, R-N.C., are both departing Congress after feuding with Trump. In Texas, Cornyn ran for re-election, losing in a primary runoff to state Attorney General Ken Paxton after Trump endorsed Paxton.
Tillis, in North Carolina, opted not to run for re-election, making his plans to retire public one day after drawing Trump’s ire for opposing a GOP-backed domestic policy package.

The two senators have partially conditioned their support for Blanche’s nomination on the Trump administration rescinding its plans for the fund, which would provide compensation for Jan. 6 rioters pardoned by Trump for claims of government overreach.
In a post on X following Trump’s statement Saturday, Tillis blamed the president for Blanche’s stalled confirmation.

“Despite comments as late as yesterday that the fund is dead, President Trump clearly intends to resurrect the payout pot for punks either by inappropriately establishing another bogus fund or pushing Congress to vote for a bill that the majority of Republicans in the Senate would be against,” he wrote.
“It’s unfortunate that Todd Blanche, who I consider qualified for the job, will not be confirmed because of this reversal. Hopefully, we can resolve this by Tuesday,” Tillis added.

Blanche’s nomination has been in jeopardy for several weeks, with Cornyn and Tillis previously saying that there are other Republican senators that share their concerns but don’t sit on the Judiciary Committee and wouldn’t have the chance to vote for or against Blanche until his nomination came to the floor.
On Wednesday night, the committee postponed a vote on Blanche’s nomination because of Cornyn and Tillis’ concerns.
On Friday, at a Cabinet meeting, the president defended the fund, saying, “It is dead, but you know, I wish it weren’t.”
“This has nothing to do with Todd,” Trump added.
The anti-weaponization fund has been blocked indefinitely by a federal judge, but the Trump administration has not pledged to stop pursuing it.

The fund was part of a settlement agreement that stemmed from a lawsuit Trump filed against the IRS. Also part of that settlement was an agreement that made the president and several family members immune from IRS audits, another provision that Cornyn and Tillis have shared concerns about.
Earlier this week, the president threatened to withdraw Blanche’s nomination and resubmit it next year, after Tillis and Cornyn have left office.

“Hey, in 158 days they can try it again, roll the dice on what the Senate confirmation process looks like next year,” Tillis told reporters at the Capitol after that threat. “It’s all on him. Certainly within his authority to do that.”

title: Nicole ‘Snooki’ Polizzi reveals hysterectomy after cervical cancer diagnosis
summary: An emotional Nicole “Snooki” Polizzi announced on Friday that she underwent a hysterectomy operation to treat Stage 1 cervical cancer, months after first disclosing her diagnosis.
story: An emotional Nicole “Snooki” Polizzi announced on Friday that she underwent a hysterectomy operation to treat Stage 1 cervical cancer, months after first disclosing her diagnosis.

The reality star, who earned fame as a hard-partying roommate on MTV’s “Jersey Shore,” announced her health scare earlier this year. Polizzi, 38, credited regular Pap smears with catching her cancer early and encouraged other women to keep up with their own exams for early detection.

Gynecologists use Pap smears to identify irregular cervical cells that can signal cancer or develop into the disease. A hysterectomy is the surgical removal of the uterus and can treat conditions ranging from cancer to endometriosis and fibroids.

“I’m going to be honest with you — not great,” Polizzi said in a TikTok post from her recovery bed. “I told you guys, in general I’m not good with pain and I’ve really been trying to be tough, but it’s not great.”

Polizzi documented her surgery experience on TikTok, from her drive to the hospital with her parents to the moment her stretcher was wheeled into the operating room. According to Polizzi, doctors also repaired her abdominal wall and performed a partial vaginal removal during the procedure.

The TV personality and businesswoman has used her platform to raise awareness about the disease and the importance of routine screening. Polizzi broke down in her video message to followers but said she was trying to stay strong.
“The nurses, they’re great. They’re saying I’m going to do fine,” she said through tears, recalling the moments before her operation. “So I lay down and I’m like, f---, it’s happening.”
“Love you! Strongest badass — it’s over and now on the road to recovery,” Polizzi’s “Jersey Shore” co-star Sammi “Sweetheart” Giancola wrote in a comment.
Pap smears are a routine, minimally invasive component of women’s health exams. When they reveal abnormal cells, physicians can monitor the situation for potential problems.
Cervical cancer rates remain a concern for researchers and advocates. The American Cancer Society found cervical cancer diagnosis rose 2% annually among women in their 30s and 40s from 2012 to 2019.

Polizzi has not publicly discussed the cause of her cancer. HPV is considered the primary cause of cervical cancers. About eight in 10 women will have an HPV infection before age 50, according to the Mount Sinai Tisch Cancer Center. Many cases of HPV resolve on their own.

title: Talking Shop (and travel essentials) with Brian Kelly, a.k.a. The Points Guy
summary: The Points Guy Brian Kelly is the top travel expert. He shares his essentials for every trip, including how he keeps his toddlers entertained on long flights.
story: Talking Shop is our series where we talk to interesting people about their most interesting buys.

No one embodies that title of “travel expert” quite like Brian Kelly, founder of The Points Guy. He’s been to every continent (multiple times, including with his toddlers) and more countries than most people visit in a lifetime. But that’s not even the most impressive part: Kelly is so well-versed in credit cards, points, miles and loyalty programs that he can book flights, hotels, excursions and more for free with his eyes closed. And for the past 16 years, he’s made it his mission to teach you how to do the same.

“I want people to have confidence traveling,” says Kelly, who took The Points Guy from a personal blog in 2010 to a multi-million dollar media company today. “I want them to be better informed and have a sense of how to navigate the system because it’s overwhelming, especially if you’re a novice traveler.”

Kelly’s role at The Points Guy has changed over the years, but at its core, it’s always revolved around helping people navigate what he calls “the complicated travel landscape.” Online, on social media and in his bestselling book, “How to Win at Travel,” Kelly shares tips about how to affordably upgrade all parts of a travel experience, and educates people about issues impacting the travel industry and what that means for upcoming trips.

Kelly’s biggest travel tip these days? Embrace flexibility, especially if you’re on a budget. “There are travel deals out there, but it’s not about booking on a Tuesday or using an IP blocker,” he says. “You need to think creatively and be flexible with dates and your destination.”

Between Kelly’s most recent adventures, I talked to him about the essentials he never forgets to add to his suitcase, how he keeps his kids entertained on flights (including to Antarctica) and the safety device he wishes more people traveled with when staying in rental homes. Read more below.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
Pak Reve Voyager Pak Family Passport Case
Kelly usually isn’t a solo traveler. His sons, ages 3.5 years old and 17 months, often go on trips with him — in fact, his youngest traveled to all seven continents by the time he was 12 months old.

To keep his family organized while going through the airport, Kelly puts everyone’s passports in this case, which has dedicated spots for different things. It also has a pen holder (Kelly keeps a pen on him at all times to make filling out forms easier) and slots for essentials like cash. “The world is more credit card-friendly, but especially while traveling internationally, having local currency and being able to tip is important,” says Kelly. “I believe in travel karma: treating people well who treat you well. That’s why I tip housekeeping at the beginning of my hotel stay, not at the end. That could dramatically improve the quality of your stay.”
Apple iPad Pro 11” (M5)

“I like to control my environment, so I always bring [my own] in-flight entertainment,” says Kelly. “Usually that’s on my iPad, which I put preloaded, downloaded content on.” Kelly also uses his iPad to plan trips. His favorite free online tool is Google Flights’ Explore. “If you’re flexible with your dates and destination, you can just say, ‘Hey, I want to get away for a weekend in September; show me where all the deals are,’” he says. “Technology is how you stay on top of it.”
Bose QuietComfort Headphones

Kelly has used these over-ear headphones to drown out noise on planes for years. They connect to his iPad and iPhone via Bluetooth, and they get up to 24 hours of battery life, which is ideal for long flights. He can also comfortably wear them for hours because they have plush ear cushions and a padded band.
On Cloud 6

“I love On Clouds,” says Kelly when I asked him about his favorite travel shoes. “For the airport, I wear a pair of white On Clouds that will look nice with slacks so I can wear them to casual dinners on my trip, and I can go to the gym in them and slip them on during the day.”
RØDE Wireless Micro

“I’m a big iPhone guy,” says Kelly. “I’ve gotten GoPros in the past, but especially while traveling with kids, I do most of my content on my iPhone. I like to use microphones, like Rode’s. They’re a really great way to elevate your content on the go and they’re easy to clip on.”
Grüns Kids

To entertain his kids while traveling, Kelly brings new toys and books to make the trip exciting, but the most important thing of all is snacks… lots of them. He and his sons are fans of Grüns’ superfood gummies, which come in kids’ and adult versions. “It’s a nice little sweet spike to just get that burst of energy when you’re tired from traveling, and they’re healthy,” says Kelly. He throws Quest’s protein peanut butter cups and SmartSweets in his bag, too.

Kelly’s other must-have while traveling with kids is a change of clothes for the whole family. “There will be delays, and there will be accidents,” he says. “It’s a matter of planning for the worst and hoping for the best.”
Kidde AA-Battery Powered CO Alarm (COBDL10)

“Since I travel with my kids, safety is a huge focus for me — it’s also one of the top questions I get asked,” says Kelly. “I take Kidde’s carbon monoxide alarm with me whenever I’m traveling, especially internationally, because it’s small, it slips into your bag and it’s battery operated, so it’s good for TSA.” (You have to take the batteries out in transit and insert them when you get to your destination.)

Kelly, who partnered with the brand to promote its Destination Safety campaign, also appreciates that this CO alarm detects low levels of carbon monoxide, which children are more vulnerable to, according to the brand.

title: Trump appeals ruling that found his $10B IRS suit aimed to ‘manipulate’ legal proceedings
summary: The case is at the center of negotiations between two Republican senators and the Justice Department over Todd Blanche’s nomination to serve as attorney general.
story: President Donald Trump on Friday took the first step in appealing a federal judge’s ruling that questioned the legality of a lawsuit filed by the president, two of his sons and the Trump Organization against the IRS.

The Trumps filed notice that they would appeal the July 13 ruling by U.S. District Judge Kathleen Williams that said the $10 billion suit was for an “improper purpose.” The case led to the Justice Department creating a $1.8 billion “anti-weaponization” fund as part of a settlement that included an agreement that the government would not investigate or seek any sort of payment from the president, his family members and companies on pending tax claims.
The IRS did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the forthcoming appeal.

A spokesperson for Trump’s legal team said Friday that the IRS “wrongly allowed a rogue, politically-motivated employee to leak private and confidential information about President Trump, his family, and the Trump Organization” to news outlets that was later “illegally released to millions of people.”
A former IRS contractor pleaded guilty in 2023 to stealing Trump’s tax records and thousands of others in 2019 and 2020 before leaking them. He is serving a five-year prison term.

The president sued the IRS and the Treasury Department in January over allegations that the agency was at fault for an unauthorized release of his tax documents that led to a report in The New York Times that said Trump had paid only $750 in federal income taxes in 2016 and 2017.
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google

In her ruling, Williams, a Barack Obama appointee, said Trump sued the IRS over his leaked tax records to “manipulate the judicial process” rather than to “vindicate rights.” She also pointed out that Trump has jurisdiction over the Justice Department, Treasury Department and the IRS.

The ruling said the Justice Department could not portray the settlement with Trump as a judicial agreement. The judge also ordered sanctions against acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, a former personal lawyer to Trump, and Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward, in addition to asking the Florida Bar Association to consider whether disciplinary action was necessary for one of Trump’s attorneys, Alejandro Brito.
The unprecedented settlement is at the center of a standoff between two Republican senators and the Justice Department that has stalled a vote on Blanche’s nomination for attorney general.

Sens. John Cornyn, R-Texas, and Thom Tillis, R-N.C., have demanded that the DOJ agree to permanently shut down the “anti-weaponization” fund and narrow the audit protection deal before they will commit to advancing Blanche’s nomination.

Trump on Friday morning acknowledged the fund is dead but told reporters, “I wish it weren’t.” He did not answer a question about whether he’d agree to limit the terms of the tax deal for himself, his family and his company.

title: Abortion is on the ballot again in these two states: From the Politics Desk
summary: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.
story: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.

In today’s edition, Adam Edelman previews two under-the-radar ballot measures that voters will decide on in next week’s primaries. Plus, our Capitol Hill team has the latest on Todd Blanche’s confirmation saga.
Sign up to receive this newsletter in your inbox every weekday here.
— Adam Wollner
Abortion is on the ballot again in two states
Following the Supreme Court’s 2022 decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, abortion rights advocates brought the fight to the states — including red ones.

That year, Kansas voters overwhelmingly struck down a proposed constitutional amendment that would have removed language enshrining abortion rights in their state — the first victory that year in what quickly became a clean sweep in six states. Two years later, Missouri voters approved a ballot initiative that effectively protected abortion rights until fetal viability — one of seven states where similar measures passed that cycle.

Next Tuesday, abortion is on the ballot again in these two states — albeit indirectly. In Missouri, one initiative on the ballot would require citizen-led constitutional amendments to secure a majority in all eight congressional districts — a significantly higher bar than the current threshold of a simple statewide majority.

In Kansas, voters will weigh in on a proposal to change how state Supreme Court justices are chosen. Currently, the governor (who since 2019 has been a Democrat) gets to appoint justices to the bench, selected from a list created by a nine-member nonpartisan commission. Tuesday’s ballot measure would instead allow for the direct election of state Supreme Court justices. In a state where registered Republicans outnumber registered Democrats 2 to 1, the proposal essentially bets that voters will reliably elect conservative — and anti-abortion — justices.

Republican legislative supermajorities in both states referred those measures to the August primary ballot — not the November general election — another bet that diminished summer voter turnout could boost their prospects of passage.

“Make no mistake about it — this is happening because the people have been winning on progressive issues,” said Chris Melody Fields Figueredo, the executive director of the Ballot Initiative Strategy Center, which works with progressive organizations to help advance citizen-led ballot measures.

In states like Kansas and Missouri that reliably elect Republicans up and down the ballot, the citizen-led ballot measure process is one of the few ways liberals have been able to score wins in recent years.
In Missouri, for example, some of the other most recent constitutional amendments passed by voters include the legalization of recreational marijuana in 2022 and Medicaid expansion in 2020.

A September analysis by Bolts magazine, which focuses on state and local politics, concluded that all five of the citizen-led ballot initiatives approved by Missouri voters since 2020 would have been rejected under the proposed threshold.

Republicans in other states are also seeking to make it more difficult for citizen-led constitutional amendments to pass. Voters in North Dakota and South Dakota will decide this fall whether to raise the requirement for passage to 60%. In Utah, voters will be asked to bump up the threshold for ballot measures specifically related to increasing taxes.
Trump defends ‘anti-weaponization’ fund, further complicating Blanche nomination

President Donald Trump defended his administration’s controversial proposal for a $1.8 billion “anti-weaponization” fund for Jan. 6 defendants and others who he says were unfairly targeted by the government.

Trump’s continued flirtation with the fund undermines assurances from his acting attorney general, Todd Blanche, and others in the administration that the idea, which faces strong opposition from some key Republicans, is dead.

It’s thrown Blanche’s nomination to be the nation’s chief law enforcement official into limbo, with two Republicans — Sens. John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina — blocking it over concerns about the settlement between Trump and the IRS that created the fund.

But Trump’s comments today are only worsening tensions with the two senators. Asked at a Cabinet meeting if the fund is dead, Trump replied: “It is dead, but you know, I wish it weren’t. To be honest with you, I think people were horribly treated, horribly abused. This has nothing to do with Todd.”
Blanche is now unlikely to be confirmed before the Senate departs next week for its five-week summer recess. The chamber is not slated to return until after Labor Day.

In a post on Truth Social earlier in the day, Trump specifically lashed out at Cornyn, suggesting that he was standing in the way of the Blanche nomination because Trump had endorsed the longtime senator’s primary challenger, Ken Paxton.
Cornyn has not directly responded to Trump’s post. But he reposted two individuals who questioned Trump’s comments on X.
